taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.source_trace: Determine who may register or modify clients and whether untrusted metadata becomes a trusted redirect, fetch destination or privileged client classification.
controls.implementation_branch: A software statement may authenticate selected metadata, not every caller-supplied field. Inspect registration update authority separately from creation. Open registration and public client classification may be intentional; escalating to a confidential/trusted client or changing another client requires a distinct observed grant.
controls.operational_method: Record any initial-access credential used for creation and the registration-access credential/client URI issued for subsequent management. Those credentials have different scopes and are not interchangeable. Compare updating the created synthetic client with attempting the same operation on a second client; successful open registration alone is not proof of cross-client update authority or confidential-client trust.
controls.controlled_verification: Use an owned local issuer and client; compare permitted registration with one unauthorized metadata mutation and inspect the effective registered client.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: Open registration can be intentional. A client identifier or reflected metadata is not client impersonation or a protected server-side fetch.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Constrain metadata and client class changes at registration/update, then verify intended public clients and rejection of privileged metadata.
